name: Urban Technology (BS)
school: Taubman College of Architecture and Urban Planning

requirements.label: 120 Total Credits
requirements.hint: The BS in Urban Technology requires 120 credits in total.

requirements.label: SI 101: Programming with Python
requirements.hint: First-fall programming course; the start of the four-course computing sequence taken in order (SI 101, SI 201, UT 435, UT 230).

requirements.label: SI 201: Data-Oriented Programming
requirements.hint: Second course in the computing sequence, taken after SI 101.

requirements.label: UT 435 & 230: Urban Informatics and Design & Urban Inquiries
requirements.hint: The second-year pair completing the in-order computing sequence. Planning UT 435 auto-places UT 230 the following winter.

requirements.label: UT 102 & 103: Anatomy of the City / Urban Observation
requirements.hint: The first-fall pair, taken alongside the Cities Intensive.

requirements.label: UT 201, 202 & 210: cities and design methods core
requirements.hint: Change-Making in Cities, Technology in Context, and Listening: Design Ethnography Methods, across years one and two.

requirements.label: Studios: UT 330, 360 & 430 (18 credits)
requirements.hint: The three 6-credit studios, taken in order across years three and four: Interaction Design & Urban Experiences, Service Design & Urban Needs, and Strategic Design & Urban Systems. Planning UT 330 auto-places UT 360.

requirements.label: UT 340, 350 & 411: Prototyping, Strategic Foresight, Becoming Digital
UT 401: Reflective Practice & Career Pathways
requirements.hint: The final-winter reflective capstone. Auto-placed after UT 430 when planning.

requirements.label: UT electives (12 credits)
requirements.hint: Four UT elective courses beyond the required curriculum.

requirements.label: First-year writing
requirements.hint: One course fulfilling the First-Year Writing Requirement.

requirements.label: Race and ethnicity (3 credits)
requirements.hint: One course carrying the Race & Ethnicity mark.

requirements.label: Statistics
requirements.hint: STATS 250 or an equivalent introductory statistics course.
